cohort: Children and young adults aged 0-24 years newly diagnosed with an intracranial tumor of neuroepithelial tissue (cases, n=49) and controls drawn from general practice lists (n=78)
finding: The study established methodologies for a future comprehensive aetiological investigation of intracranial tumors in children and young adults, finding that cases were less likely to be breastfed and more likely to be delivered by caesarean section and have a birthweight > 3.5 kg compared to controls.
mod_finding: Cases were more likely to be delivered by caesarean section than controls (OR 1.6; 95% CI 0.6-4.4).
